questions.questionText: A signal is sampled at 8000 Hz and a 256‑point DFT is computed. What frequency in Hertz does bin k = 20 correspond to?
questions.explanation: The bin frequency is f_k = k·f_s/N = 20·8000/256 = 20·31.25 = 625 Hz.

questions.questionText: A continuous‑time signal contains frequency components up to 8 kHz. What is the minimum sampling rate that guarantees no aliasing according to the Nyquist criterion?
questions.explanation: Nyquist requires f_s > 2·f_max, so f_s must exceed 2·8 kHz = 16 kHz; the smallest rate satisfying this is 16 kHz.

questions.questionText: A continuous‑time signal contains a sinusoidal component at 7 kHz. If the signal is sampled at a rate of 10 kHz, at what frequency will this component appear in the discrete‑time (sampled) spectrum due to aliasing?
questions.explanation: Aliasing folds frequencies above f_Nyquist (5 kHz) back into the baseband: f_alias = |f_original – k·f_s|. Here, 7 kHz – 1·10 kHz = –3 kHz, whose magnitude is 3 kHz.

questions.questionText: If a signal is sampled at f_s = 10 kHz and a 512‑point DFT is computed, what is the frequency spacing Δf between adjacent DFT bins?
questions.explanation: Δf = f_s / N = 10,000 Hz / 512 ≈ 19.531 Hz, which rounds to 19.53 Hz.

A continuous‑time signal contains frequency components up to 15 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the minimum sampling rate that must be used to avoid aliasing?
questions.explanation: To prevent aliasing the sampling rate f_s must satisfy f_s > 2 f_max. Here f_max = 15 kHz, so the smallest integer rate that meets the condition is just above 30 kHz; the standard choice is 30 kHz.

questions.questionText: According to the Nyquist‑Shannon Sampling Theorem, what is the minimum sampling frequency f_s required to sample a continuous‑time signal whose highest frequency component is f_max = 3 kHz without incurring aliasing?
questions.explanation: The Nyquist‑Shannon theorem states that to avoid aliasing the sampling frequency must be at least twice the highest frequency present in the signal (the Nyquist rate). For f_max = 3 kHz, the minimum f_s is 2 × 3 kHz = 6 kHz.

questions.questionText: According to the Nyquist‑Shannon Sampling Theorem, what is the minimum sampling frequency required to sample a continuous‑time signal whose highest frequency component is 15 kHz without causing aliasing?
questions.explanation: The sampling rate must be strictly greater than twice the highest frequency (f_s > 2·f_max). For f_max = 15 kHz, 2·f_max = 30 kHz, so any rate just above 30 kHz (e.g., 30.1 kHz) satisfies the criterion.

questions.questionText: A signal is sampled at a rate of 44.1 kHz. What is the highest analog frequency that can be represented without aliasing?
questions.explanation: The Nyquist frequency equals half the sampling rate: f_Nyquist = f_s / 2 = 44.1 kHz / 2 = 22.05 kHz. Frequencies above this will fold (alias) into the baseband.

questions.questionText: A continuous‑time signal is sampled at a rate of f_s = 8 kHz and a 16‑point DFT is computed from the sampled data. What is the frequency spacing Δf between adjacent DFT bins?
questions.explanation: Δf = f_s / N = 8000 Hz / 16 = 500 Hz. This is the spectral resolution of the DFT.
